dimensions.assessment: Affects all vehicle manufacturers selling light vehicles in the U.S. and all road users including pedestrians and cyclists.
dimensions.evidence: automatic emergency braking system installed in any passenger motor vehicle manufactured for sale in the United States

dimensions.assessment: Mandates changes to vehicle safety design and sensor capabilities across future vehicle fleets.
dimensions.evidence: detect and respond to a bicyclist, motorcyclist, other cyclist, or other vulnerable road user

dimensions.assessment: Imposes regulatory compliance and manufacturing costs on automakers, though specific federal fiscal outlays are not detailed.
Amends federal motor vehicle safety standards and mandates a new federal rulemaking process.
dimensions.evidence: Section 30129 of title 49, United States Code, is amended... the Secretary shall initiate a rulemaking process

dimensions.assessment: Permanent federal vehicle safety standards affecting all future vehicle production past the compliance deadlines.
dimensions.evidence: The compliance date of the revised rule... shall be not later than 2 years after the date on which the revised rule is issued.

missing_information: Estimated cost per vehicle for consumers or manufacturers.
Exact federal administrative costs for the rulemaking process.
importance_detail.rationale: Directs the Department of Transportation to initiate a rulemaking process to strengthen automatic emergency braking standards for light vehicles regarding vulnerable road users.
